name: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
venue: UIST 2023 (36th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology, UIST '23, San Francisco, CA). arXiv:2304.03442 (v1 submitted 7 Apr 2023, v2 6 Aug 2023). DOI 10.1145/3586183.3606763.
authors_affiliation: Joon Sung Park, Joseph C. O'Brien, Carrie J. Cai, Meredith Ringel Morris, Percy Liang, Michael S. Bernstein. Primary affiliation: Stanford University (Park, O'Brien, Liang, Bernstein); Google Research / Google DeepMind (Cai, Morris).
code_url: https://github.com/joonspk-research/generative_agents (official, Apache-2.0; the 'reverie' simulation backend + Django 'Smallville' frontend). ~21.5k stars.
maintained_repo_url: N/A (single research repo, last updated Aug 2023; no continuously-maintained leaderboard or paper list).
task_domain: Interactive multi-agent simulation of believable human behavior (embodied/social agents in a sandbox world). Not a QA/tool-use/code benchmark task; the agent must remember, reflect on, and plan day-to-day behavior in a Sims-like town (Smallville) and engage in social interaction.
problem_setting: Interactive, open-ended, MULTI-AGENT setting: 25 generative agents populate a sandbox game world (Smallville) and run continuously for two simulated days. Each agent is a frozen LLM (gpt-3.5-turbo / ChatGPT) wrapped with a memory-stream architecture; there is no task reward or ground-truth label and no model training. Supervision is essentially absent (no gradient updates); behavior is driven entirely by prompting the LLM with retrieved natural-language memories. Agents perceive each other and the environment, write every experience to a private growing memory stream, and use retrieval to condition planning and reaction. End users can also inject natural-language interventions (e.g. 'throw a Valentine's Day party').
what_is_retrieved: experiences / memories: natural-language memory records from a per-agent 'memory stream'. These are (a) observations (events the agent directly perceives), (b) reflections (higher-level synthesized inferences the agent generates about itself/others), and (c) plans (intended future action sequences). The retrieved units are passed into LLM prompts to ground reactions, conversations, planning, and reflection.
retrieval_grounding: GROWING / episodic memory the agent writes. Retrieval targets each agent's own continuously-growing memory stream (a complete first-person natural-language log of experiences) rather than a static external corpus, KB, or API set. No fixed document corpus is indexed; the store expands at every time step of the simulation.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Top-k ranking by a composite relevance score, but k is budget-driven rather than a fixed rank: the highest-scoring memories are retrieved and as many as fit within the LLM context window are included. The objective is to surface the most pertinent memories for the current situation/query, not a learned ranking metric (no Recall@k/nDCG objective is optimized); there is no explicit minimal-set-completeness objective.
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve: yes, Reuse: partial, Revise: no, Retain: yes]. The system Retrieves relevant past memories and Retains all new experiences (and synthesized reflections) in the memory stream, but does not implement classic CBR case Reuse-via-adaptation or Revise-then-store of a solution; reflection is a synthesis/abstraction step rather than CBR case adaptation. (Approximate mapping; the work is not framed as CBR.)
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner. It describes a 'memory stream' + retrieval + reflection + planning architecture for believable agents, not a CBR cycle.
retrieval_unit: experience record / memory object: a single natural-language memory entry in the memory stream. Each is a typed record (observation, reflection, or plan) with a timestamp, a most-recent-access timestamp, a natural-language description, and a precomputed embedding. Reflections are higher-abstraction memory objects that point to the evidence memories they were synthesized from (forming a tree of citations).
index_source: Growing memory, online/test-time-induced: the retrievable store is the agent's memory stream, which is constructed entirely online during the simulation (each perceived event, generated reflection, and plan is appended). Optionally seeded with an authored 'seed memory'/agent-history paragraph at initialization, but the bulk of the index grows at deployment time. Not an offline-induced static corpus.
index_structure_topology: Flat append-only list (a chronological 'memory stream') with per-record metadata (creation timestamp, last-access timestamp, importance score, embedding). Reflections add a shallow tree/citation structure (a reflection links to the lower-level memories it abstracts), but the primary store is a flat time-ordered log scored at query time. No external vector DB / graph DB / hierarchical category index.
retriever_type: Hybrid heuristic scorer (not a trained retriever): a hand-designed weighted combination of (i) dense relevance via cosine similarity between memory embeddings and the query embedding, (ii) recency via exponential time decay, and (iii) importance via an LLM-generated salience score. The dense-similarity component uses off-the-shelf LLM-produced embeddings; recency and importance are non-learned signals fused with the similarity score.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf / hand-designed). The retriever is not trained: relevance uses frozen pretrained embeddings; recency uses a fixed exponential-decay factor (0.995); importance uses the LLM's own 1-10 rating prompt. The three normalized components are combined with equal weights (alpha_recency = alpha_importance = alpha_relevance = 1) in the released implementation. No contrastive, LM-feedback, RL, or downstream-effectiveness training of the retriever.
query_construction: The query is a natural-language description of the agent's current situation. For reactions, the agent's current observation/situation is used as the query memory. For reflection, the agent first generates (via the LLM) a small set of salient high-level questions about its recent experiences, and each question becomes a retrieval query. Queries are embedded with the same embedding model used for memories. Query construction is thus situation-conditioned and, for reflection, LLM-synthesized.
query_granularity: Step/state-level (situation-level): a fresh retrieval query is constructed at each decision point as the agent's current situation/observation changes, and again whenever reflection is triggered or a plan must be (re)generated. Not a single one-shot query at t=0.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative / event-driven: retrieval is invoked repeatedly throughout the simulation whenever the agent must (a) decide how to react to a newly perceived observation, (b) hold a conversation, (c) generate or revise a plan, or (d) reflect. Triggering is by the simulation loop and by the importance-sum reflection threshold, not by a learned router or token-confidence signal.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Event/schedule-driven plus a threshold heuristic for reflection: (i) for reaction/conversation/planning, retrieval is triggered when a new observation is perceived or a plan step is needed (agent/environment-initiated); (ii) reflection-triggered retrieval fires when the sum of importance scores of the agent's most-recent perceived events exceeds a fixed threshold (150 in the implementation, yielding ~2-3 reflections per day). No token-level confidence, attention-uncertainty, or learned complexity classifier.
reranking: No separate second-stage reranker (no cross-encoder / RRF / instruction-tuned reranker). The single composite score (normalized recency + importance + relevance, equal weights) directly ranks memories; the top-scoring set within the context budget is selected.
retrieved_context_refinement: Minimal: top-ranked memories are selected by the composite score and truncated to fit the LLM context window; there is no learned distillation, decompose-recompose, or distractor filtering of the retrieved memories themselves. Higher-level synthesis happens upstream via reflection (which compresses raw observations into abstract statements that are then stored and later retrievable), not as a post-retrieval refinement step.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tool/skill documents are indexed; the store holds natural-language experience memories, not API/tool descriptions).
index_content_separation: Partial / implicit: each memory's natural-language description and its precomputed embedding serve as a lightweight retrievable key, and the full record text is loaded into the prompt only when selected. There is no explicit progressive-disclosure SOP-index-then-content design; it is a single-tier memory stream.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (not a tool-retrieval system; no RapidAPI/RESTful/MCP/function-calling tool registry or CRUD auto-sync). The 'live' aspect is that the memory stream is continuously appended during simulation.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no tools/APIs and thus no inter-tool dependency modeling).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: retrieved memories are inserted as natural-language context into LLM prompts that produce the agent's next action/reaction, conversation utterances, daily plan and its recursive decomposition, and reflection statements. Memory thus grounds moment-to-moment behavior, dialogue, and planning. No training signal or latent-token injection; the frozen LLM consumes retrieved memories as text.
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-plan with hierarchical, recursive top-down decomposition, plus retrieval-conditioned reactive replanning. At plan time the agent retrieves its summary description and prior-day summary to generate a broad-stroke daily agenda, then recursively decomposes it into hour-long chunks and then 5-15 minute fine-grained actions. During execution, each new observation triggers retrieval to decide whether to continue the plan or react/replan (and reflections feed back into subsequent planning). Retrieval is woven in at multiple planning levels (subtask/situation level), not a single one-shot exemplar injection and no tree search/MCTS.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-action / per-situation within the ongoing simulation rollout: retrieval is interleaved at each perceive-retrieve-act decision point and at each (re)planning and reflection event, rather than per-CoT-token. Effectively per-step over a long-horizon multi-day rollout.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A for classic CBR adaptation. Retrieved memories are used as in-context natural-language evidence; the LLM synthesizes new behavior/reflections from them (LLM-prompted synthesis) rather than adapting a retrieved solution case verbatim. No execution-feedback case revision, critic-guided revision, or RL reuse-finetuning.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw natural-language memory text. Observations are raw event descriptions; reflections are LLM-distilled higher-level statements (still natural language); plans are natural-language future-action descriptions. Injected as plain text into prompts. No executable program/skill, structured note schema, or latent/soft tokens.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Mixed: raw observation records (low abstraction) AND distilled reflections/insights (high abstraction) coexist in the same stream and are retrieved together. Reflections are LLM-synthesized abstract inferences about self/others; observations are concrete single events; plans are procedural future-action descriptions.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Implicit only: the composite recency+importance+relevance score is intended to surface salient, pertinent memories and down-weight stale/irrelevant ones, reducing distractors in the prompt. There is no retriever-aware training, learned relevance evaluator, self-reflection-as-filter, or reason-in-documents refinement to explicitly guard against incorrect retrieved context.
memory_type: episodic (per-agent 'memory stream' of observations) augmented with a synthesized semantic/abstract layer (reflections) and a procedural layer (plans). Long-term, natural-language, persistent within a simulation; private per agent.
write_back: True. Every perceived observation is appended to the memory stream; the LLM-generated reflections and plans are also stored back as new memory objects, so the store accumulates both raw experience and synthesized abstractions during the simulation.
online_growth: Yes. The memory stream grows continuously at test/deployment time as the simulation runs (every observation, reflection, and plan is appended). The store is not frozen after any offline induction.
write_back_trigger: Per-step / continuous for observations (every perceived event is written immediately). Reflections are written reflectively, triggered when the summed importance of recent events crosses the threshold (150), producing ~2-3 reflections/day. Plans are written when generated/decomposed and updated when the agent replans in reaction to observations. Writes are not conditioned on task success/failure (there is no task reward).
failure_experience_usage: N/A in the success/failure sense: the simulation has no task-level success/failure signal, so memories are not labeled success vs. failure. All experiences (including socially 'unsuccessful' interactions) are stored uniformly as observations; there is no failure-specific corrective rule store or success-vs-failure contrastive retrieval.
memory_evolution_update: Primarily append-only, with two evolving dynamics: (1) reflection creates new higher-level memory objects abstracted from existing ones (link-and-evolve / abstraction over time), and (2) each memory's 'last-access' recency timestamp is updated when retrieved, which mutates its future recency score. Existing memory descriptions are not overwritten, deduped, or pruned/forgotten in the released system.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval is a fixed, hand-weighted heuristic top-k over recency+importance+relevance (no M-MDP, soft Q-learning, RL, or any learned selection policy). The only 'learned' component is the pretrained embedding model used for the relevance term.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No shared memory store: each of the 25 agents has its own PRIVATE memory stream. Information spreads between agents only via in-world social interaction (one agent's utterance becomes another agent's observation), i.e. emergent diffusion through conversation, not a shared retrievable index or cross-framework memory.
benchmarks: No standard ML benchmark. Two custom human-grounded evaluations on the Smallville sandbox: (1) a controlled individual-agent evaluation in which agents are interviewed with questions across 5 categories (self-knowledge, memory, plans, reactions, reflections; five questions per category) and human raters rank believability via TrueSkill; (2) an end-to-end two-game-day community simulation of 25 agents measuring emergent social behaviors (information diffusion, relationship/network formation, coordination around a Valentine's Day party). Base LLM: gpt-3.5-turbo (ChatGPT).
benchmark_family: Custom interactive multi-agent social-simulation / believability evaluation (embodied-sandbox flavor, Sims-inspired 'Smallville'). Does not fit the standard QA / web / embodied-RL / tool / code / memory-benchmark families; closest descriptor: human-evaluated believability of LLM agent behavior in an open-ended simulated society.
baselines: Internal ablations of the architecture serve as the comparison conditions, plus a human upper-bound: (a) Full architecture (observation + planning + reflection); (b) No reflection; (c) No reflection, no planning; (d) No observation, no planning, no reflection (minimal LLM agent); (e) Human Crowdworker condition (crowdworkers author the agent's responses given the same memory/role information) as a human-authored baseline.
key_metrics: Controlled study: TrueSkill skill rating (mean mu, std sigma) of believability from human pairwise comparisons over interview responses. End-to-end study: emergent social-behavior measures: information-diffusion counts/percentages, social-network density, and coordination success (fraction of invitees who attend). Qualitative behavior/believability analysis and failure-mode discussion.
headline_result: In the controlled believability evaluation (TrueSkill, human pairwise ranking), the full generative-agent architecture ranked highest (mu = 29.89, sigma = 0.72), and ablating components monotonically reduced believability: No reflection mu = 26.88; No reflection + no planning mu = 25.64; No observation + no planning + no reflection (memory-less) mu = 21.21. The full architecture also outperformed the Human Crowdworker condition (mu = 22.95, sigma = 0.69). End-to-end, from a single user-seeded intent the agents autonomously spread a Valentine's-party invitation to 13 of 25 agents (4% to 52%), spread Sam's mayoral candidacy to 8 of 25 (4% to 32%), grew network density from 0.167 to 0.74, and coordinated so that 5 of 12 invited agents actually showed up to the party.
ablations: The central result IS an ablation: a TrueSkill comparison of Full architecture (mu=29.89) vs. No reflection (mu=26.88) vs. No reflection + no planning (mu=25.64) vs. No observation + no planning + no reflection (mu=21.21), demonstrating that observation/memory, planning, and reflection each contribute critically and additively to believability; the memory-less condition is worst and even below the human-crowdworker baseline (mu=22.95). Qualitative failure analysis notes issues such as memory retrieval missing relevant records, embellishment/hallucination of memories, and overly formal/cooperative ChatGPT-style speech. (No intrinsic Recall@k retrieval ablation.)
evaluation_decoupling: No. Intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / completeness) are not reported separately. Evaluation is entirely on downstream behavior quality (TrueSkill believability ranking) and emergent social outcomes; retrieval quality is only discussed qualitatively in the failure analysis.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both, in a behavior-quality sense: the controlled study scores the quality/believability of the agent's responses (a process/behavior judgment via interviews) rather than a single task outcome, and the end-to-end study measures emergent process outcomes (diffusion, relationship formation, coordination). There is no reasoning-faithfulness or step-wise retrieval-accuracy metric.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Discussed qualitatively rather than tabulated: the authors note that running the simulations with many agents over multiple days was time-consuming and costly (each agent issues many LLM calls per simulated step; 'could be somewhat costly, especially when there are many agents'). No explicit per-call token cost, latency table, or accuracy-vs-cost curve is reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Budget-capped top-k: memories are ranked by the composite score and the highest-ranked are included up to the LLM's context-window limit (no fixed numeric k is mandated by the method; selection is reranked-then-truncated to fit the prompt). Recursive planning produces fixed-grain decompositions (daily -> hour-long -> 5-15 minute chunks). No adaptive precision-driven k.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A as a released benchmark, but for completeness: the evaluation world is a custom Sims-inspired sandbox ('Smallville') with 25 agents simulated over two game days; the controlled study uses interview questions in 5 categories (5 questions each) with human TrueSkill ranking; the released repo ships base simulations (base_the_ville_n25 with 25 agents and a 3-agent base) and authored seed-memory CSV history files.
builds_on: Large language models as the cognitive core (ChatGPT / gpt-3.5-turbo); chain-of-thought and LLM prompting; prior LLM-agent and reasoning-and-acting work (e.g. ReAct-style reason-act loops, social-simulacra / interactive-agent work by the same group); cognitive-architecture notions of memory, retrieval, and reflection; cosine-similarity dense retrieval over text embeddings; TrueSkill ranking for human-judgment aggregation; The Sims as the interaction/world-design inspiration.
contrasts_with: Rule-based / scripted NPC and finite-state-machine game agents (which lack open-ended believable behavior); cognitive-architecture agents requiring hand-built symbolic procedures; and plain LLM agents without long-term episodic memory, retrieval, planning, or reflection (its own ablated memory-less condition, which performs worst). Also contrasts with reinforcement-learned game agents that optimize a task reward, whereas this work has no reward and targets believability.
lineage: Foundational work in the experience/episodic-memory lineage of retrieval-augmented LLM agents (group D, case-based / experience-based planning): it popularized the 'memory stream' with retrieval scored by recency + importance + relevance plus reflection, a template later adopted/extended by many memory-augmented and experience-replay agent frameworks (e.g. reflection/insight-distillation agents, generative-agent simulations, and LLM agent memory modules). Sits upstream of works that turn experience retrieval into a learned policy or add success/failure-contrastive memory.
